_comment: Pinned SatNOGS observations. Day 3 fetches exactly these, so the Doppler validation is reproducible. Narrowband CW telemetry beacons near 435 MHz: the cleanest carrier to track. Four are pinned rather than one so a noisy capture can be dropped without re-selecting, and so the residual structure can be compared across four different ground stations and four TLE ages. Selected 2026-09-05 from network.satnogs.org with status=good; every field below is copied from the observation record, not typed by hand.

observations.note: Highest-elevation CW beacon in the selection. Primary.
The station tuned 2000 Hz above the transmitter's nominal downlink. That offset is in the record, so it is a known constant to subtract rather than a mystery in the residual.
The only capture whose TLE comes from CalPoly rather than Space-Track. Kept deliberately: a different TLE provider is a different residual.
Same station as TISAT-1, three hours later. Two passes from one receiver isolate a station clock offset from a per-satellite TLE error.

_provenance: The TLE current at capture is not stored here. It is carried on the observation record itself and written to satnogs/captures/<id>/tle.txt by satnogs/fetch.py, so the TLE used for the comparison is always the one the station used, never a fresher one fetched later.
